Tunisian Olive Oil in Singapore: A First-Pass Market Study

A desk-research exercise using trade data and Singapore's official import guidance to find out what needs checking before anyone recommends market entry.

Status
Completed
Category
Market research
Started
2026-10-16
Updated
2026-10-16

The question

Could a Tunisian olive-oil producer find a place in Singapore? I chose a real product and a real destination so I could work with evidence instead of a country-level checklist. This is a first-pass desk study, not a recommendation to export.

I used an AI assistant to help locate and organise public sources. The source links are included so the figures can be checked directly. I have not interviewed Singaporean buyers, contacted an importer, audited supermarket shelves, or obtained shipping quotes.

What the numbers say

The World Bank's WITS page, using UN Comtrade data, reports Singapore's 2024 imports of olive oil under HS 1509 at 2,795,220 kg worth US$25.50 million. The figures below are reported values unless marked as a calculation.

ItemFindingHow to read it
Singapore, total imports in 20242,795,220 kg; US$25.50 millionA real import market exists, but this total includes different olive-oil products and does not tell me what any one segment will pay.
Spain1,704,470 kg; US$15.83 millionAbout 61.0% of reported import volume.
Italy884,710 kg; US$7.44 millionAbout 31.6% of reported import volume.
Spain and Italy togetherAbout 92.6% of volumeCalculated from the reported quantities. This suggests a market with established suppliers, not an easy opening.
Tunisia130 kg; about US$1,800A very small recorded flow in this dataset, around 0.0046% of total volume. It does not prove that Tunisian oil could not sell there.
Average import valueAbout US$9.12 per kg overallCalculation: total declared value divided by total quantity. This is not a retail price or a supplier quote.
Tunisia's recorded unit valueAbout US$13.85 per kgCalculation from only 130 kg. The quantity is too small to use as a sensible pricing benchmark.

Source: WITS / UN Comtrade, Singapore olive-oil imports in 2024. Figures and percentages are rounded. The page uses HS 1509, so the figures should not be treated as an extra-virgin-only market estimate.

Regulatory facts to check early

Singapore's Food Agency says businesses importing processed food for commercial sale must be registered with SFA and must obtain the relevant import permit through TradeNet. Importers also need to meet Singapore's food rules. Before making a shipment, the exact product category, code, labelling and supporting documents should be confirmed for the oil and packaging in question.

Source: Singapore Food Agency, import of food for commercial sale.

Singapore's IRAS explains that import GST is 9% of the applicable taxable value, which includes the cost, insurance and freight value and any customs duties payable. A real landed-cost model would need a freight quote, the correct customs classification, importer charges and advice on how GST applies to the business. The percentage alone is not the total cost of entry.

Source: IRAS, importing goods.

Facts, estimates and unanswered questions

TypeCurrent noteNext check
FactSingapore imported about 2.80 million kg of HS 1509 olive oil in 2024.Confirm the product segments and check whether a newer full-year data set is available.
FactSpain and Italy account for most of the reported volume.Compare brands, origins, pack sizes and shelf prices in Singapore stores.
FactTunisia's recorded quantity in the data is only 130 kg.Check whether this was a one-off consignment, a reporting quirk, or a broader pattern across years.
EstimateA product would need to compete with established origins on some combination of price, quality, provenance, packaging or buyer relationships.Ask importers which of those things would actually change their buying decision.
UnknownRetail prices, importer margins, shipping cost per bottle, insurance, packaging cost, shelf life and likely order size.Obtain local shelf observations and quotes; do not fill these cells with invented numbers.
UnknownWhether Singaporean buyers would seek a Tunisian brand at a viable price.Speak to potential importers or retailers and test their interest in a specific offer.

What I can conclude so far

The broad question, "Does Singapore import olive oil?", has a clear answer: yes. The next question is harder. The 2024 data show a market dominated by Spanish and Italian supply and almost no recorded Tunisian volume. That is a reason to investigate the barrier to entry, not evidence on its own that the idea will succeed or fail.

I would not recommend entering the market yet. The next useful work would be a small shelf-price comparison, two or three conversations with importers, a supplier specification for a defined Tunisian product, and a landed-cost estimate based on real shipping and importer quotes. Until then, there is no defensible selling price or margin to present.

Sources

  • WITS / UN Comtrade: Singapore olive-oil imports, 2024
  • Singapore Food Agency: requirements for importing food for commercial sale
  • IRAS: GST on imported goods

Desk research prepared 16 October 2026. Trade data refer to 2024; regulatory details should be rechecked before any commercial decision.
